t: Cusco was occupied by the Killke people from about 900, became the capital of the Kingdom of Cusco and then of the Inca Empire, and was planned round two channelled rivers, four quarters and roads to the four provinces.
The Spanish entered the city in November 1533, plundered its palaces and temples and built a new city on Inca walls; Manco Inca besieged it for ten months in 1536 and failed.
Earthquakes in 1650 and 1950 destroyed much of the colonial city, and the Inca walls that withstood them are now visible again.
dyk: When the earthquake of 1950 damaged more than a third of the city's structures, Inca architecture withstood it, and the damage exposed granite retaining walls of the Qurikancha that had been hidden.
ev: The Killke build the walled complex of Sacsayhuamán
Generals of Atahualpa capture Cusco from the supporters of Huáscar at the Battle of Quipaipan
Francisco Pizarro arrives in Cusco on 15 November
The Spanish re-establish the city on 23 March
Manco Inca besieges Cusco for ten months and then retreats to Vilcabamba
An earthquake destroys almost all the colonial buildings
Túpac Amaru II besieges Cusco and is later executed in the Plaza de Armas
An earthquake on 21 May damages more than a third of the city's structures

f.founded: In the 12th century by Manco Cápac, according to Inca tradition; the Killke people occupied the region from 900 to 1200 and built the fortress of Sacsayhuamán about 1100
f.where: In the central Andes of south-eastern Peru, at about 3,400 metres, between the Huatanay and Urubamba rivers, near the Sacred Valley
f.known: Capital of the Inca Empire; the Qurikancha, the Temple of the Sun; Sacsayhuamán; Inca stonework used as the base of the Spanish city; the siege of 1536; the Cusco School of painting; earthquakes; the Inti Raymi festival
f.today: Cusco is the capital of the Cusco Province and Department of Peru, an archbishopric, and a World Heritage Site since 1983.
